title: Remote Work: Permanent Home-Working vs. Full-Time Office Return
sourceNotes: Naskah orisinal tim Success IELTS, tidak diambil dari buku atau tes resmi manapun.
prompt:
Some people believe that employees should be allowed to work from home permanently, while others think employees should return to the office full-time.

Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

Write at least 250 words.
sampleAnswer:
The question of whether employees should work from home permanently or return to the office full-time has become increasingly debated since many companies experimented with remote arrangements. While both positions have merit, I believe a balanced approach is generally preferable to either extreme.

Those who support permanent home-working point to several genuine advantages. Employees save considerable time and money by not commuting, which can improve both productivity and personal wellbeing. Many parents and carers also find it easier to manage family responsibilities when they are not required to be physically present in an office every day. Furthermore, some studies suggest that certain tasks, particularly those requiring deep concentration, are actually completed more efficiently at home, away from office interruptions.

On the other hand, advocates of a full-time office return argue that face-to-face interaction cannot be fully replaced by video calls. Spontaneous conversations between colleagues often lead to creative problem-solving and informal mentoring that rarely happen over a screen. New employees, in particular, may struggle to learn company culture and build professional relationships without regular in-person contact. There are also concerns that permanent remote work can blur the boundary between personal and professional life, leading to longer, less structured working hours.

In my view, neither extreme is ideal for most organisations. A hybrid model, in which employees spend some days in the office and some working remotely, captures the main benefits of both approaches: it preserves opportunities for collaboration and mentoring while still offering flexibility and reduced commuting. Policies should ultimately depend on the nature of the work and the preferences of individual teams, rather than being applied rigidly to every employee.

In conclusion, while home-working offers flexibility and office-based work supports collaboration, a combination of the two is likely to serve most employees and employers better than either option alone.
